prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1134; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a rear-end collision at a stop light and stated neck pain began within hours. Claim opened and assigned for review.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant's vehicle at the scene and records the rear impact as described. Driver is named on the policy and coverage was active at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who gave the same account of the collision as in the first report. No earlier injury to the neck or upper back appears in the file.

Entry 4: Witness statements and scene photos match the described sequence of events. The other driver confirmed the impact and did not dispute how it happened.

Entry 5: Inspected the claimant's vehicle. Rear bumper and trunk damage is consistent with the force of the reported impact. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded in the file, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 6: Claimant was referred for medical evaluation and diagnosed with whiplash. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course of physical therapy and home exercises. Claimant reports steady improvement and fewer restrictions on daily activities.

Entry 8: Checked prior claims and medical history for the same body area. No earlier injury to the neck or back is known.

Entry 9: Follow-up call with claimant. Symptoms have tapered as expected, and the treating provider notes the recovery is on track for the usual timeline.

Entry 10: Reviewed the full file. Liability, vehicle damage, injury, and treatment all line up with the reported loss. Recommending the claim proceed to settlement review.
